propositions: Current audit window spans 68 days (2026-06-08 through 2026-08-15) across 2,265 work tickets (713 tasks, 684 stories, 648 bugs, 220 epics) with 92.9% closure rate; median lead time 0.48 days and median cycle time 1.52 hours represent high throughput but do not establish sustainable flow or quality.

Plan-review adoption rose from 29.2% (Q2 review-before-claim) to 79.5% (Q3), first-pass PASS rate is 49.0% with p90 attempts at 8, and completion first-pass is 72.3%; testing-section tickets scored 79.7% first-pass versus 68.6% without, but causal effect is unproven.

No current bug has detected_by metadata (7 of 648 = 1.1% have the optional field), making true escaped-defect rate and detection-stage efficiency unavailable; caused_by links are advisory and demonstrably noisy with blame-attribution false-positive risk.

Code-review first-pass rate is 97.4% (1,178/1,209) but this describes the observed funnel, not reviewer effectiveness or escaped-defect prevention; caused_by-linked sources showed initial plan PASS only at 30.3% versus 49.5% for others (small-N selection effect).

Commit process governance reached near-complete adoption in Q3 (ticket trailer 90.4%, DCO 82.9%, Change-Id 99.3%); source diff size decreased (median 111.5→95 lines) and test co-change increased (median 84.5→160.5 lines) from Q2 to Q3, supporting process maturation.

Thirty-five source modules are at or above 720 LOC (15 at or above 780, 4 at 797-800), duplication is 4.09% (1,826 clones), and 47.7% of consecutive same-file touches occur within 24 hours; these identify debt pressure and coordination hotspots but do not prove causation to defects.
